newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan picks Merrill Lynch to advise telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: Jordan picks Merrill Lynch to advise telecom sale.

text.p: Jordan has picked Merrill Lynch as adviser in the proposed sale of 26 percent of the state's profitable Jordan Telecommunications Co, Minister of Communications Jamal Sarayrah said on Monday.
"Today the privatisation committee agreed on the choice of Merrill Lynch International to undertake this operation," Sarayrah told reporters.
He said Merrill Lynch was chosen from a shortlist of five candidates. It will advise the government on the sale of the telecommunications stake to a strategic investor.
"Their proposal was very clear, transparent, and it was cheap," Sarayrah said, without giving details.

The telecommunication sale is one of two major planned government sell-offs which form the vanguard of Jordan's IMF-approved privatisation programme. In October Sarayrah said the sale should go ahead by the end of 1997.
Industry officials say the telecoms business in Jordan offers huge potential in a country with around 400,000 telephone lines and a population of over four million.
The government is also preparing to sell a similar stake in mainly state-owned Jordan Cement Co.
